banner: DRAFT growth stages. Lengths are FAO's general examples for four broad stages, not a local forecast and not checked by an agronomist. Your variety, planting date and weather can shift them by weeks. Use them as a guide and confirm with your extension officer.

source.name: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (Crop evapotranspiration), Chapter 6, Table 11: lengths of crop development stages
source.caveat: FAO says these values are useful only as a general guide and are average lengths for the regions and periods named, intended as examples; local observation should be used wherever possible.

stages.name: Early growth
stages.what: From planting until the young crop starts to cover the ground.
stages.tip: Small plants use little water. Check that seedlings have come up evenly.

stages.name: Crop development
stages.what: The crop grows fast and covers more of the ground each week.
stages.tip: The crop is using more water each week. Check soil moisture.

stages.name: Mid-season
stages.what: The crop is at or near full cover. This period often includes flowering.
stages.tip: Usually the period of highest water use, and it often includes flowering. Check soil moisture often.

stages.name: Late season (ripening)
stages.what: Leaves begin to age and yellow and the crop ripens towards harvest.
stages.tip: The crop is ripening. Plan your harvest, drying and storage.
